title: Notice the observer
line: Five minutes with the one in you who watches.
intro: Logos, Athena says, is not thinking but the one who observes: something in you always watches what you live. In Athena’s reading of Heraclitus, the ever-living fire is this Logos, primordial consciousness, one and common to all. For five minutes, notice the watcher, and rest as it.
does: Sit for five minutes and notice what in you watches your thoughts and senses.
trains: Recognising the observer, the logos, behind everything you live.

steps.text: Sit comfortably with your back upright. Close your eyes, or let them rest on the floor, and take three slow breaths.
Notice what you are living right now: the sounds in the room, the weight of your body, a thought passing. Change nothing.
Now notice that something in you is watching all of it. The sounds come and go; the watching stays.
When a thought comes, see it rise and pass. You have the thought; you are the one who observes it.
Athena calls this observer logos: not thinking, but the energy of consciousness, Heraclitus’ ever-living fire. Rest as the one who watches.
Heraclitus says the Logos is ξυνός, common to all. The same watching looks out through everyone you will meet today.
Come back slowly: feel your hands and feet, open your eyes, and take the watching with you into the day.
